_about: Intended-behavior descriptions for the ss_intent condition, one per ORIGINAL (pre-mutation) program, built by i-corpus-construction/3-build_intent_descriptions.py. source: 'mbpp' = MBPP problem statement for the task id; 'clover' = CloverBench docstring; 'written' = hand-written from the original program (intent_written.json). Docstring level: purpose and key behavior in plain English, no Dafny syntax, formulas or exact bounds. original_text keeps a real description verbatim; edited=true means description is a docstring-level rewrite of it because the original failed the text check. Set reviewed to true only after a co-author checks the text; prompts refuse to build for programs without a reviewed description.

630-dafny_tmp_tmpz2kokaiq_Solution.description: Binary search over a sorted integer array. Given a value, it returns a position where that value occurs, or a special not-found result if the value does not appear in the array.

AssertivePrograming_tmp_tmpwf43uz0e_DivM.description: Arithmetic on unary natural numbers, built from zero and a successor constructor, with conversions to and from ordinary naturals, comparison, addition, subtraction and multiplication. The main method performs iterative division with remainder of one unary number by a nonzero one, returning the quotient and the remainder. Helper lemmas relate these operations to each other.

AssertivePrograming_tmp_tmpwf43uz0e_Find.description: Searches a string for the first occurrence of another string. It reports whether the second string occurs inside the first, and when it does, returns the starting position of an occurrence. Helper predicates and lemmas describe the progress of the nested search loops.

AssertivePrograming_tmp_tmpwf43uz0e_Merg.description: Recursive merge sort on an integer array. It returns a new array of the same length that is sorted and holds exactly the same elements as the input. A merge routine combines two sorted arrays into a destination array whose size is the sum of theirs, keeping the result sorted and preserving all elements.

CS494-final-project_tmp_tmp7nof55uq_bubb.description: Bubble sort for a non-empty integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order. The result contains the same elements as the original. Helper predicates describe a sorted range of the array and the position of the largest element during each pass.

CS5232_Project_tmp_tmpai_cfrng_LFUSimple.description: A least-frequently-used cache with a fixed capacity that maps integer keys to values and tracks how often each key is used. Looking up a key returns its value and updates its use count, or a special missing-key result if the key is absent, without adding or removing keys. Inserting a value may evict the least frequently used key, which a helper method finds.

CVS-Projto1_tmp_tmpb1o0bu8z_Hoare.description: Small Hoare-logic exercises. One method returns the larger of two natural numbers, another returns some value related to two ordered positive inputs, one computes Fibonacci numbers iteratively, one sums a linked list, and one finds the largest element of a non-empty array.

CVS-Projto1_tmp_tmpb1o0bu8z_proj1_proj1.description: Range sums over an integer array. A query method computes the sum of the elements between two positions, and a fast version answers the same query using a precomputed prefix-sum array. A second part converts a non-empty array into a linked list containing every element of the array.

CVS-handout1_tmp_tmptm52no3k_1.description: Range sums over an integer array. A query method computes the sum of the elements between two positions directly, and a fast version answers the same query in constant time using a precomputed prefix-sum array. A lemma splits a range sum into two adjacent parts.

CVS-handout1_tmp_tmptm52no3k_2.description: Converts an array into a linked list. The resulting list has the same length as the array, holds the array's elements in the same order, and contains no value that is not in the array.

Clover_array_product.original_text: Calculate the pair-wise product of two arrays.
Clover_array_product.description: Calculate the pair-wise product of two arrays.

Clover_array_sum.original_text: Calculate the pair-wise sum of two arrays.s
Clover_array_sum.description: Calculate the pair-wise sum of two arrays.s

Clover_binary_search.original_text: Binary search a sorted possibly empty array for a key. Return the index such that array[index-1] < key <= array[index].
Clover_binary_search.edit_reason: original states the exact index bounds as a formula
Clover_binary_search.description: Binary search a sorted, possibly empty array for a key. Return the position at which the key would be inserted to keep the array sorted.

Clover_cal_sum.original_text: Calculate the sum from 1 to N. Require that N is a non-negative integer. Return the sum.
Clover_cal_sum.edit_reason: original states the exact starting bound of the sum (a spec literal)
Clover_cal_sum.description: Calculate the sum of the integers up to N, for a non-negative integer N. Return the sum.

Clover_canyon_search.original_text: Calculate the smallest difference of any two values from two non-decreasing arrays. Require that two input arrays to be non-empty and sorted. Ensure that the return value exists as one difference and is the smallest one.
Clover_canyon_search.description: Calculate the smallest difference of any two values from two non-decreasing arrays. Require that two input arrays to be non-empty and sorted. Ensure that the return value exists as one difference and is the smallest one.

Clover_copy_part.original_text: Copies `len` elements from `src` array starting at `sStart` to `dest` array starting at `dStart` and returns the modified `dest` array. Ensure r and dest have the same length. Ensure original `dest` elements outside copied range stay the same.
Clover_copy_part.description: Copies `len` elements from `src` array starting at `sStart` to `dest` array starting at `dStart` and returns the modified `dest` array. Ensure r and dest have the same length. Ensure original `dest` elements outside copied range stay the same.

Clover_has_close_elements.original_text: Check if in given list of numbers, are any two numbers closer to each other than given non-negative threshold.
Clover_has_close_elements.description: Check if in given list of numbers, are any two numbers closer to each other than given non-negative threshold.

Clover_linear_search2.original_text: Linearly search for an element in a possibly empty array and return the index of its first appearance. Require that the input array contains the element. Ensure the returned index is the first appearance of the element.
Clover_linear_search2.description: Linearly search for an element in a possibly empty array and return the index of its first appearance. Require that the input array contains the element. Ensure the returned index is the first appearance of the element.

Clover_linear_search3.original_text: Linearly search for an existing element that satisfies a predicate in an array. Return the index of its first appearance. Require that the input array contains such an element. Ensure that no previous elements satisfy such predicate.
Clover_linear_search3.description: Linearly search for an existing element that satisfies a predicate in an array. Return the index of its first appearance. Require that the input array contains such an element. Ensure that no previous elements satisfy such predicate.

Clover_match.original_text: Input strings p and s are of equal length. Return true if, for every character in s, it matches the corresponding character in p or the character in p is a wildcard '?'.
Clover_match.description: Input strings p and s are of equal length. Return true if, for every character in s, it matches the corresponding character in p or the character in p is a wildcard '?'.

Clover_max_array.original_text: Returns the maximum value m present in the array a. Ensure that such an element appears in the array and is the maximum element.
Clover_max_array.description: Returns the maximum value m present in the array a. Ensure that such an element appears in the array and is the maximum element.

Clover_min_array.original_text: Return the value of the minimum element in a non-empty array. Ensure that such an element appears in the array and is the minimum element.
Clover_min_array.description: Return the value of the minimum element in a non-empty array. Ensure that such an element appears in the array and is the minimum element.

Clover_online_max.original_text: Require that the input array to be non-empty and x is an non-zero index into the array. Return the index of the first element that is strictly larger than m, the maximum element in the first x elements, or return the last index. Ensure the returned index is larger than or equal to x. Ensure the ghost variable represents the largest element in the first x elements of the array (DO NOT use max).
Clover_online_max.edit_reason: original names a ghost variable and states exact index bounds
Clover_online_max.description: Given a non-empty array and a position x inside it, compute the largest element m among the elements before x. Return the index of the first later element that is larger than m, or the last index if there is none.

Clover_quotient.original_text:
Find the quotient and remainder of a division of a dividsor and a dividend. 
Require the dividend to be non-zero.
Ensure that the divisor equals to quotient times dividend plus remainder. Ensure that the quotient and remainder are positive. Ensure the remainder less than th dividend.
Clover_quotient.edit_reason: original states the division equation and the remainder bound in words (formula), which the text check cannot detect
Clover_quotient.description: Find the quotient and remainder of dividing one natural number by a nonzero one.

Clover_remove_front.original_text: Removes the front element from the array a and returns the resulting array c.
Clover_remove_front.description: Removes the front element from the array a and returns the resulting array c.

Clover_rotate.original_text: Rotate the array by the offset to the left.
Clover_rotate.description: Rotate the array by the offset to the left.

Clover_slope_search.original_text: Search for the index of an existing key in a slope represented by an 2-D array. Require the slope to be a plane whose height is non-decreasing on the same x-axis (horizontal line) or same y-axis (vertical line). Require that such an element exists.
Clover_slope_search.description: Search for the index of an existing key in a slope represented by an 2-D array. Require the slope to be a plane whose height is non-decreasing on the same x-axis (horizontal line) or same y-axis (vertical line). Require that such an element exists.

Clover_two_sum.original_text:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the first pair of indices i < j of the two numbers such that they add up to target. 
Require that such pair (i , j) exist in the array. 
Ensure for all i less than returned i and for all j, that no other i, j exists.
Ensure for all j between returned i j, no other j exist.
Clover_two_sum.edit_reason: original states index ordering with an operator and spells out the minimality conditions
Clover_two_sum.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the first pair of indices of two numbers that add up to target. Require that such a pair exists in the array.

Correctness_tmp_tmpwqvg5q_4_MethodCalls_.description: Computes Stern's diatomic sequence (the fusc function) for a non-negative input. The function is described through its recursive rules for even and odd arguments, and the method computes the value iteratively.

Correctness_tmp_tmpwqvg5q_4_Sorting_Tang.description: Given two sorted arrays of integers, determines whether some value of the first array also appears in the second, using binary search over the second array. The binary search returns the position where a value would be inserted, splitting the array into smaller and not-smaller elements.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session1.description: Given a non-empty array and a position in it, returns whether the position acts as a barrier: the elements on its left side are all smaller than the elements on its right side. It runs in linear time.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session2.description: Three ways to compute the integer square root of a non-negative number: a linear search upward, a slower search, and a binary search. All three return the same result.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session3.description: Several methods for finding the maximum of a non-empty array. Some return the position of a maximum element, including variants that return the first or the last such position, and others return the maximum value itself, which must occur in the array.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session4.description: Checks whether all elements of an array are equal. Several lemmas show equivalent formulations of the property (comparing all pairs, comparing to the first element, or comparing neighbours), and five methods implement the check in different ways.

Given two strictly increasing arrays, returns whether every element in a prefix of the first array also occurs in a prefix of the second array. The lengths of both prefixes are given as inputs, and the method runs in linear time.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session5.description: Computes the sum of the elements of an integer array. Two recursive definitions of the sum, adding from the left and from the right, are proved to agree on any slice, and two methods compute the sum with loops.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session6.description: Counts how many elements of an array of non-negative integers are even, matching a recursive counting function.
Counts how many times the minimum value occurs in a non-empty array, in a single pass, matching recursive definitions of the minimum and of the number of occurrences.
Sums the peaks of a non-empty array, where a peak is an element that is a running maximum: nothing before it is bigger. The method computes this sum in linear time, matching a recursive definition.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session7.description: Binary search on a sorted array, in iterative and recursive versions. It returns the boundary position for the searched value, that is, where the value sits or would sit in the sorted order. Further methods use it to decide whether the value occurs in the array, and to return a matching position when it does.

Two bubble sort variants that sort a segment of an integer array in place. Afterwards the segment is sorted, contains the same elements as before, and the parts of the array outside the segment are unchanged.
Selection sort on a segment of an integer array, in place. Afterwards the segment is sorted, contains the same elements as before, and the parts of the array outside the segment are unchanged.

Rearranges an integer array so that all non-negative elements come first and all negative elements come after them. It returns the position where the negative part begins, and the result is a permutation of the original array.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session8.description: Insertion sort on an integer array, in place. Afterwards the array is sorted in ascending order and contains the same elements as before.

Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session9.description: Given a non-empty integer array and a position in it, finds the largest sum of a contiguous segment that ends at that position. It returns the sum together with the starting point of a best segment. Two versions exist, one scanning left to right and one scanning right to left.

Dafny-Grind75_tmp_tmpsxfz3i4r_problems_t.description: The classic two-sum problem: given a sequence of integers and a target, return a pair of distinct positions whose values add up to the target. The input is assumed to contain such a pair.

Dafny-Practice_tmp_tmphnmt4ovh_BST.description: Binary search trees over integers. One method builds a search tree from a sequence without duplicates, so that the tree holds exactly the numbers of the sequence; another inserts a new number into a search tree, keeping it a search tree. A tree is a search tree when its in-order traversal is strictly ascending.

Dafny-demo_tmp_tmpkgr_dvdi_Dafny_BinaryS.description: Binary search for a key in a sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the key when the key is present, and a negative result when the key does not occur in the array.

Dafny-experiences_tmp_tmp150sm9qy_dafny_.description: Finds the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.

DafnyExercises_tmp_tmpd6qyevja_Part1_Q1.description: Adds two integer arrays of the same length element by element and returns the resulting array.

DafnyPrograms_tmp_tmp74_f9k_c_map-multis.description: A multiset of integers specified abstractly and implemented with a map from elements to their counts. Adding an element always adds a copy of it; removing an element deletes one copy if present and otherwise leaves the multiset unchanged, and both report whether anything changed. Other operations return the size, compare two multisets for equality and list the elements.

DafnyPrograms_tmp_tmp74_f9k_c_prime-data.description: A database that records which natural numbers are prime. Numbers can be inserted either as known primes or after testing their primality, and a lookup answers Yes, No or Unknown depending on whether the number is stored and whether it is prime, without changing the database. A helper tests primality directly.

DafnyProjects_tmp_tmp2acw_s4s_findMax.description: Finds the maximum value in a non-empty array of real numbers.

Dafny_Learning_Experience_tmp_tmpuxvcet_.description: Counts the even numbers in a prefix of a sequence, both directly and using a precomputed array of running counts. Other methods fill in that precomputed array, build a two-dimensional table from an array, and multiply two non-negative integers by repeated addition.

Linear search variants. The generic search returns the first position whose element satisfies a predicate, or a not-found result when none does. Other variants search a prefix of an array, or look for a given element and report its position in a one-based style, or not found.

Two stacks sharing a single fixed-capacity array, one growing from each end. Each stack supports push, which reports failure when the shared space is full, pop and peek, which report failure when that stack is empty, and emptiness and fullness checks. A validity predicate ties the abstract stacks to the shared array.
Searches the first part of an array for a given natural number. It returns a one-based position where the element was found, or a not-found result, together with the number of elements examined.

A checksum calculator that keeps a string and a running checksum of it, defined as the sum of the character codes reduced modulo a fixed prime. Appending text updates the stored string and its checksum; the data and the checksum can be read back.

Dafny_Programs_tmp_tmp99966ew4_binary_se.description: Binary search for a value in a sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the value when present, and a negative result when the value does not occur.

Dafny_Programs_tmp_tmp99966ew4_lemma.description: Finds a zero in an array of non-negative integers whose values never drop sharply from one position to the next. Because of this, the search can skip ahead by the current value, and a lemma justifies the skip. It returns the position of a zero, or a negative result if there is none.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_AI_agent_va.description: Small verification examples: computing a power of two iteratively, finding the maximum of an array of naturals (with a default when the array is empty), cubing a number, incrementing every entry of a matrix, copying one matrix into another of the same shape, doubling every element of an array into another array, and rotating an array left or right by one position.

warnings: number word 'two' (2 is a spec literal)

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_AI_agent_ve.description: Computes a power of two iteratively for a non-negative exponent, matching a recursive definition.
Copies every entry of a source matrix into a destination matrix of the same shape.
Writes twice each element of a source array into a destination array of the same length.

warnings: number word 'twice' (2 is a spec literal)

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_AI_agent_ve.description: Rotates a non-empty array to the right by one position in place, so the last element moves to the front and every other element shifts one place towards the end.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Fine_Tune_E.description: A loop benchmark: starting from two equal non-negative inputs, it counts both down together until they reach the counter, and returns the final values. The goal is to show that the two values stay in step.

A loop benchmark: it walks through the numbers up to a positive limit and, at arbitrary steps, remembers the current number. The goal is to show that the remembered number is always a valid index below the limit.

A loop benchmark: it counts up to a non-negative limit, increasing one counter at every step and a second counter at every other step. The goal is to show the relationship between the two counters when the step count is even.

warnings: number word 'two' (2 is a spec literal)

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Fine_Tune_E.description: A loop benchmark: it counts up to a non-negative limit while accumulating a running total of the counter. The goal is to show a lower bound on the final values in terms of the limit and an extra parameter.
Binary search on a sorted integer array that returns the insertion point of a key, the position where the key belongs in the sorted order.
Computes the sum of all elements of a non-empty integer array, matching a recursive definition of the sum of a prefix.
Finds the maximum of the first part of an integer array, whose length is given.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Generated_C.description: A loop benchmark: it decreases a starting value once for each step up to a limit and returns it. The goal is to show a bound on the result.
Counts how many times a value occurs in the first part of an integer array, matching a recursive counting function.
Finds the minimum value of a non-empty integer array.
Multiplies two non-negative integers using repeated addition.
Starting from the product of two non-negative numbers, repeatedly subtracts one of them while counting the other down, and returns what is left, which should end at zero.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Test_Cases_.description: Basic loop exercises over a non-negative bound: counting up to the bound with two different loop conditions, counting down to zero with two different loop conditions, and computing a quotient by repeated subtraction.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_dataset_C_c.description: A loop benchmark translated from C: for a given non-negative number of steps, it increases two counters by small amounts, choosing arbitrarily at each step which counter gets the larger increase. The goal is to show how the counters' total relates to the number of steps.
A loop benchmark translated from C: for a positive input, it repeatedly adds a fixed step to an accumulator once per count up to the input, and returns the accumulator.
A loop benchmark translated from C: it decreases a starting value once for each step up to a limit and returns it. The goal is to show a bound on the result.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_dataset_bql.description: Finds the minimum among the first elements of an integer array, where the number of elements to consider is given.
Adds up the first elements of an integer array whose elements are bounded by a given maximum. The goal is to show that the total is bounded accordingly.
Computes the square of a non-negative integer using repeated addition.

Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_dataset_err.description: Decides whether a non-negative integer is even, matching a recursive definition that alternates between even and odd.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 1_Li.description: Searches a segment of a sequence for a value, once recursively and once with a loop. Each version returns the last position in the segment holding the value, or a not-found result if the value does not occur in the segment.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 2_Bi.description: Binary search, recursive and iterative, over a segment of a sequence of reals sorted in descending order. It returns the position where the searched value belongs in that order.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 3_In.description: Insertion sort that turns a multiset of integers into a sorted sequence with exactly the same elements. A binary search helper finds where a value belongs in a sorted sequence.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 3_Se.description: Selection sort that turns a multiset of integers into a sorted sequence with exactly the same elements. A helper returns the smallest value of a non-empty multiset.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 8_H8.description: Quickselect on multisets. Partition picks a pivot from a non-empty multiset and splits the remaining elements into those on either side of the pivot. QuickSelect uses it to find the element of a given rank, returning it along with the elements that come before and after it in sorted order.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_tests_Search1000.description: Bentley's fixed-size binary search from Programming Pearls, applied to the sorted beginning of a large array. It returns the position where the searched value belongs. Further versions, iterative and recursive, handle sorted segments whose size has a special power-of-two form.

Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_tests_SumIntsLoop.description: Computes the sum of the positive integers up to a non-negative bound with a loop. The result matches a recursive definition and the usual closed-form formula.

Dafny_tmp_tmpmvs2dmry_examples2.description: Arithmetic exercises on naturals: addition by repeated increments, multiplication by repeated addition, the greatest common divisor of two positive numbers by repeated subtraction, and raising a non-negative real to a natural power by repeated squaring.

Dafny_tmp_tmpmvs2dmry_pancakesort_findma.description: Part of pancake sort: returns the position of a largest element within the first part of a non-empty array, whose length is given. The array's contents are not changed.

Dafny_tmp_tmpmvs2dmry_pancakesort_flip.description: Part of pancake sort: reverses the beginning of a non-empty array up to a given position, in place, leaving the rest of the array unchanged.

Dafny_tmp_tmpv_d3qi10_2_min.description: Returns the smaller of two integers, both as a function and as a method, and finds a minimum element of a non-empty integer array.

Dafny_tmp_tmpv_d3qi10_3_cumsum.description: Computes the cumulative (prefix) sums of a non-empty integer array into a second, distinct array of the same length, so that each entry of the second array holds the sum of the input up to that position.

FMSE-2022-2023_tmp_tmp6_x_ba46_Lab10_Lab.description: A bounded list that may only contain odd integers. It supports inserting at a position or at either end while capacity remains, removing an element or the element at a position, popping from either end, reading the length and the element at a position, binary search on a sorted list, and merging two sorted lists. Every operation keeps the capacity fixed and the list valid.

Final-Project-Dafny_tmp_tmpmcywuqox_Atte.description: Increments every element of a non-empty integer array by one, in place.
Finds the maximum of a non-empty array of non-negative integers and returns both its value and a position where it occurs.
Binary search for a value in a non-empty sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the value, or a position outside the array if the value is not present.
Sorts an integer array in place into ascending order. A helper finds the position of the smallest element in the remaining part of the array, starting from a given position.
Insertion sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order.

Quicksort on integer sequences. A threshold helper splits a sequence into the elements on either side of a pivot value, keeping every element exactly once. The sort returns a sequence with the same elements as its input.

FlexWeek_tmp_tmpc_tfdj_3_reverse.description: Iteratively builds a new character array holding the elements of a non-empty input array in reverse order. The input array is not modified.

Formal-Verification-Project_tmp_tmp9gmws.description: String utilities with matching specification predicates: checking whether one string is a prefix of another, whether one string occurs as a substring of another, whether two strings share a common substring of a given length, and finding the length of the longest common substring. Lemmas show that each property and its negated form are complementary.

Formal-Verification_tmp_tmpuyt21wjt_Dafn.description: String utilities with matching specification predicates: checking whether one string is a prefix of another, whether one string occurs as a substring of another, whether two strings share a common substring of a given length, and finding the length of the longest common substring. Lemmas show that each property and its negated form are complementary.

Formal-methods-of-software-development_t.description: Introductory exercises: methods that return a pair of values built from an input and a positive offset, computing factorials iteratively in two ways, and computing the square of a positive number by summing consecutive odd numbers, with a lemma relating that sum to the square.

warnings: number word 'two' (2 is a spec literal)

Formal_Verification_With_Dafny_tmp_tmp5j.description: A stack of integers with limited capacity, stored in an array. It supports initialisation with a positive capacity, an emptiness check, peeking at and popping the top element of a non-empty stack, pushing onto a stack that is not full, shifting all elements down by one, and a second push that discards the oldest element when the stack is full.

HATRA-2022-Paper_tmp_tmp5texxy8l_copilot.description: Binary search on a sorted array of distinct integers. It returns the position of the target when present, and a not-found result otherwise.

Finds the largest sum of any contiguous subarray of a non-empty integer array (Kadane's algorithm). A predicate states that the result is the maximum over all subarray sums, and a recursive function sums a range of the array.

Sorts an integer array of moderate size, returning an array sorted in ascending order with the same elements as the input. Helper predicates describe a sorted range and a pivot position used during sorting.
The two-sum problem on an array: given an array that contains two entries adding up to a target, return two different positions whose values add up to the target.

warnings: number word 'two' (2 is a spec literal)

M2_tmp_tmp2laaavvl_Software Verification.description: Counts up from zero with a loop until reaching a non-negative input, and returns the final count, which equals the input.

MFES_2021_tmp_tmpuljn8zd9_FCUL_Exercises.description: Linear search for a key in a non-empty integer array. It returns a position holding the key, or the array length when the key is not found.

MFES_2021_tmp_tmpuljn8zd9_PracticalClass.description: Sorts an integer array in place using insertion sort. Afterwards the array is in ascending order and holds the same elements as before.

MIEIC_mfes_tmp_tmpq3ho7nve_TP3_binary_se.description: Finds a value in a sorted integer array with binary search and returns its position, or a not-found result if the value is absent.

MIEIC_mfes_tmp_tmpq3ho7nve_exams_mt2_19_.description: Partitions a non-empty array around a chosen pivot by reordering its elements, placing them on either side of the pivot according to how they compare with it. It returns the pivot's final position, and the array keeps the same elements.

MIEIC_mfes_tmp_tmpq3ho7nve_exams_special.description: Uses binary search to find where a value can be inserted into a sorted array so that it stays sorted. The array itself is not changed.

Program-Verification-Dataset_tmp_tmpgbdr.description: Higher-order array exercises: filling an array so that each entry is a given function applied to its position, and a sorting routine that orders an array according to a supplied comparison function.

Finds a maximum element of a non-empty array of any type, using a supplied comparison that is total and transitive. The result is an element of the array that compares as at least as large as every element.
Insertion sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order.

Multiplies two integer matrices whose inner dimensions agree. The result has as many rows as the first matrix and as many columns as the second, and each entry is the product of the corresponding row and column.

Euclid's proof that there are infinitely many primes. For any number there is a larger prime, and no finite set contains every prime; the proof builds a new prime from the product of a set of primes. A model of crash-consistent memory updates using an undo log. Fast exponentiation of naturals by repeated squaring, using the binary representation of the exponent. Helper functions convert numbers to and from bit sequences, and lemmas relate exponents of sums to products and describe how appending bits changes the value.

Computes sums of cubes of consecutive integers over a range, and from zero up to a bound. Lemmas relate sums over ranges, show that the sum of the first cubes equals the square of the corresponding triangular number, and give the closed form of that triangular number.

A deceptively simple sorting algorithm that runs two nested loops over all pairs of positions and swaps the two elements whenever the first position comes before the second and the order calls for it. dafny-workout_tmp_tmp0abkw6f8_starter_ex.description: Returns the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.

dafny_examples_tmp_tmp8qotd4ez_leetcode_.description: LeetCode's sqrt: returns the integer square root of a non-negative integer. A lemma shows that the integer square root is unique.

LeetCode's find the celebrity: among a small group of people, a celebrity is someone everyone else knows who knows no one else. The method returns the celebrity if there is one, or a not-found result otherwise, eliminating candidates in one pass and then checking the remaining one.

dafny_examples_tmp_tmp8qotd4ez_test_shuf.description: Shuffles an array: returns a new array of the same length containing the same elements in random order, using a random-number helper that returns a value in a range and a swap helper. Lemmas relate multisets, sets and membership in sequences.

dafny_projects_tmp_tmpjutqwjv4_tutorial_.description: Exercises from the Dafny online tutorial: Fibonacci numbers, linear search and binary search returning a position or a negative not-found result, updating a sequence, finding a zero in an array whose values never drop sharply using a skipping lemma, counting true values in a boolean sequence, and paths in a closed graph.

dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_GenericSe.description: Generic selection sort over any element type with a supplied less-than comparison. Sorting leaves the array ordered and holding the same elements, and a measurable comparison operation counts how many comparisons are made, which stays within a quadratic bound in the array length.

dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_Selection.description: Selection sort on an integer array, in two versions, sorting it in place into ascending order. Helper predicates state that a range is ordered and that the array's elements are preserved.

dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_minmax2.description: Returns the difference between the largest and the smallest element of a non-empty integer array, using recursive definitions of the minimum and maximum of a sequence.

dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_realExpon.description: Axiomatised real powers and logarithms with a positive base. Lemmas state that power and logarithm undo each other, that the logarithm of a product is a sum of logarithms, and how the power grows when the exponent increases by one. A method computes the power for a positive natural exponent by repeated multiplication.

feup-mfes_tmp_tmp6_a1y5a5_examples_Selec.description: Selection sort on an array of reals, sorting it in place into ascending order and keeping the same elements. A helper finds the position of a minimum value in a non-empty range of the array.

formal-methods-in-software-engineering_t.description: Lab exercises on Hoare logic: a Hoare triple about updating a running square, loop rules with assumptions and invariants, the sum of the squares of the naturals up to a bound with a lemma giving its closed form, and integer division with remainder of a non-negative number by a positive one.

formal-verification_tmp_tmpoepcssay_stri.description: String utilities with matching specification predicates: checking whether one string is a prefix of another, whether one string occurs as a substring of another, whether two strings share a common substring of a given length, and finding the length of the longest common substring. Lemmas show that each property and its negated form are complementary.

formal_verication_dafny_tmp_tmpwgl2qz28_.description: The Bulls and Cows game: given a secret and a guess of the same short length, each made of distinct natural numbers, count the bulls (right number in the right place) and the cows (right number in the wrong place). Recursive functions define both counts.

Sorts a non-empty sequence of DNA bases into the order A, C, G, T, adapting the Dutch national flag algorithm to four values. A helper swaps two positions of a sequence, and the result has the same bases as the input.

fv2020-tms_tmp_tmpnp85b47l_modeling_conc.description: Models a ticket-based mutual exclusion protocol in which processes cycle through thinking, hungry and eating. A process takes a ticket when it becomes hungry, may eat when its ticket is being served, and advances the serving number when it leaves. A lemma proves that no two processes eat at the same time, and run methods schedule processes repeatedly.

ironsync-osdi2023_tmp_tmpx80antoe_linear.description: C++ compilation tests for arrays of unsigned integers: returning a null or a small fresh array, linear search that returns the first position of a key or the length when it is absent, and printing arrays.

laboratory_tmp_tmps8ws6mu2_dafny-tutoria.description: Returns the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.

llm-verified-eval_tmp_tmpd2deqn_i_dafny_.description: A HumanEval problem: given a string, if it contains any letters, flip the case of every letter and leave other characters alone; if it contains no letters, return the string reversed. Helper functions identify letters, toggle case, and reverse a sequence.

A HumanEval problem: given a non-empty sequence of integers, return the sequence of rolling maxima, where each entry is the largest value seen up to that position. A helper finds the maximum of a non-empty sequence.

metodosFormais_tmp_tmp4q2kmya4_T1-Metodo.description: Computes the sum of all elements of an array of naturals, matching a recursive function that sums a prefix.

pucrs-metodos-formais-t1_tmp_tmp7gvq3cw4.description: A queue of integers stored in an array that starts with a small default capacity and grows when full. It supports reporting its size and whether it is empty, adding to the back, removing from the front of a non-empty queue, testing membership, and concatenating two queues.

se2011_tmp_tmp71eb82zt_ass1_ex4.description: Computes the square of a non-negative integer.

software_analysis_tmp_tmpmt6bo9sf_ss.description: Selection sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order so that the result is a permutation of the original. A helper returns the position of a minimum element within a non-empty range of the array.

specTesting_tmp_tmpueam35lx_examples_bin.description: Specification testing for binary search on a sorted sequence. The original specification returns a position holding the key or a negative result when it is absent; a deterministic version also fixes the not-found result and requires the first matching position; deliberately wrong variants and transition predicates are used to test whether specifications are strong enough.

summer-school-2020_tmp_tmpn8nf7zf0_chapt.description: Tests whether a natural number greater than one is prime by checking its possible divisors with a loop, matching a predicate defining primality.
Merge sort on integer sequences. Merging two sorted sequences produces a sorted sequence with the elements of both, and the sort returns a sorted sequence with the same elements as its input.

t1_MF_tmp_tmpi_sqie4j_exemplos_colecoes_.description: Computes the sum of all elements of an array of naturals, matching a recursive function that sums a prefix.

Deletes a run of characters from a line of text stored in a character array: the characters before the deleted part stay the same and the characters after it shift left to close the gap. The line's length and the deleted range must fit within the array.

tangent-finder_tmp_tmpgyzf44ve_circles.description: Given an array of circle radii and a sorted array of positions on a line, all non-negative, decides whether some radius equals some position, which corresponds to a circle being tangent to a line.

test-generation-examples_tmp_tmptwyqofrp.description: A set of integers stored as a sequence without duplicates. It can be created empty or from a duplicate-free sequence, report its size, add or remove an element (leaving the set unchanged when the element is already present or absent), test membership, and compute intersections and unions.

veri-sparse_tmp_tmp15fywna6_dafny_concur.description: A proof of concept for concurrent matrix-vector multiplication: each process is assigned one row of the matrix and accumulates that row's product with the vector one column at a time. Lemmas about sums of sequences support the proof that the output vector is the full product once all processes finish.

veri-sparse_tmp_tmp15fywna6_dafny_dspmsp.description: Multiplies a sparse matrix in compressed form by a sparse vector, producing a dense result vector of the matrix's row count. Each entry of the result is the sum of products over the coordinates that the matrix row and the vector have in common. Helper functions look up coordinates and compute minima.

veri-sparse_tmp_tmp15fywna6_dafny_spmv.description: Multiplies a sparse matrix in compressed sparse row form by a dense vector. The result has one entry per row, and each entry is the sum of the row's stored values times the matching vector entries.

verified-using-dafny_tmp_tmp7jatpjyn_lon.description: Finds the longest run of consecutive zeros in a non-empty integer array, returning its length and starting position. Every longer stretch of the array contains a non-zero element.

vfag_tmp_tmpc29dxm1j_sumar_componentes.description: Computes the sum of all components of an integer array, matching a recursive function that sums the array from a given position to the end.
